question: Should OpenClaw fail closed for all nine newly listed wrapper names, accepting that previously approved or allowlisted wrapper invocations will be denied until OpenClaw can reason about their child command?
rationale: This is an intentional command-policy boundary change: the code pattern is established, but maintainers must choose the upgrade and security posture for existing wrapper-based workflows.

options.title: Confirm fail-closed classification
options.body: Retain all verified unmodeled command carriers as opaque wrappers and record the intentional approval/allowlist behavior change before merge.

options.title: Narrow to contract-verified carriers
options.body: Remove any entry whose invocation grammar OpenClaw can already parse safely or whose command does not dispatch a child executable.

options.title: Add parsers for common transparent cases
options.body: Implement narrow parser-backed unwrap support for wrappers whose stable documented grammar permits correct child-command resolution.

recommendation.title: Confirm fail-closed classification
recommendation.body: Retain all verified unmodeled command carriers as opaque wrappers and record the intentional approval/allowlist behavior change before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the spec-driven wrapper semantics and trust-plan refactors that define the affected policy boundary.
